domain_label: Probability & Statistics Mastery (Mathematical & Symbolic Reasoning Specialization subdomain)
assumptions: no observed dataset or benchmark evidence supplied; all scores are heuristic priors
subdomain scope is probability and statistics competency for math specialist LLMs; excludes linear algebra, calculus, and numerical methods
evaluation targets both theoretical derivation ability and practical pitfall avoidance
key references: Blitzstein & Hwang (Introduction to Probability), Wasserman (All of Statistics), Casella & Berger (Statistical Inference)
exclusions: measure-theoretic probability beyond CLT and MCMC convergence
time series econometrics and spectral analysis
experimental design beyond power analysis and blocking

competency_questions.question: What is the sample space, and how are probability axioms used to verify a valid probability measure?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PROB_FOUND defines axioms and sample space

competency_questions.question: How are discrete vs continuous random variables defined and what determines choice of PMF vs PDF?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: RV_DIST covers PMF/PDF/CDF for both types

competency_questions.question: How does Bayes' theorem update a prior belief given evidence, and what is the risk of ignoring the base rate?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: BAYES_THM and COND_PROB jointly explain prior-to-posterior update

competency_questions.question: How are expectation and variance computed for standard named distributions, and what is the law of total expectation?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: EXP_VAR and RV_DIST define E[X] and Var(X) for named families

competency_questions.question: What does the Central Limit Theorem guarantee, and when does the approximation break down?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: LLN_CLT states conditions and Berry-Esseen caveats

competency_questions.question: How are MLE and MOM estimators derived, and what properties (bias, consistency, efficiency) should be verified?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: POINT_EST covers MLE/MOM derivation and property checks

competency_questions.question: How are Bayesian credible intervals constructed and how do they differ semantically from frequentist confidence intervals?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: BAYESIAN_INF and INTERVAL_EST together cover both with explicit distinction

competency_questions.question: What are Type I and Type II errors, and how is test power computed and controlled?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: HYPO_TEST covers error types; MULTITEST covers multiplicity

competency_questions.question: How are regression coefficients interpreted under OLS assumptions, and what diagnostics detect assumption violations?
How is Simpson's paradox identified and what structural causal reasoning resolves it?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PITFALLS and CAUSAL_INF cover paradox identification and resolution

competency_questions.question: How does MCMC sampling work and what convergence diagnostics confirm reliable posterior samples?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SAMPLING and BAYESIAN_INF cover MCMC mechanics and R-hat

competency_questions.question: What is a Bayesian network and how is d-separation used to read off conditional independencies?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PROB_MODELS covers BN, d-separation, and Markov blankets

competency_questions.question: How should LLM evaluation benchmarks be statistically designed to detect real performance differences?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PROB_LLM covers power analysis and multiple comparison correction for LLM benchmarks

competency_questions.question: What canonical pitfalls (p-hacking, survivorship bias, ecological fallacy) must a practitioner guard against?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PITFALLS enumerates and explains each pitfall with mitigations

glossary.definition: Kolmogorov's three axioms: non-negativity, normalization, countable additivity
P(data|parameter) treated as function of parameter with data fixed
P(parameter|data) obtained via Bayes' theorem from prior and likelihood
probability under null hypothesis of observing test statistic at least as extreme as observed
frequentist interval with coverage guarantee P(CI contains true param)>=1-alpha over repeated sampling
maximum likelihood estimator; parameter value maximizing P(data|theta)
KL(P||Q)=E_P[log(P/Q)]; asymmetric non-negative divergence between distributions
T(X) is sufficient for theta if P(X|T(X),theta) does not depend on theta
1-P(Type II error)=P(reject H0|H1 true); probability of detecting a real effect

source_registry.description: heuristic prior estimates for probability and statistics competency work units; grounded in Blitzstein & Hwang, Wasserman, and Casella & Berger syllabi without observed benchmark data
grounding_limits: domain-general heuristic priors based on probability/statistics pedagogical literature

nodes.definition: Master sample spaces, events, axioms of probability, counting methods, and combinatorial probability to correctly assign likelihoods to outcomes.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: foundational curriculum revision or introduction of measure-theoretic framing

pros.claim: Anchors all downstream probability calculations in rigorous axiomatic foundation

cons.claim: Deceptively simple axioms hide deep subtleties (uniform vs non-uniform spaces)

failure_modes: conflating equally-likely outcomes with uniform probability
off-by-one in counting arguments
acceptance_tests: axioms stated correctly with non-negativity, unity, countable additivity
classic counting problems solved exactly (birthday, coupon collector)
revisit_triggers: combinatorics syllabus changes
new probability paradox surfaces in practitioner literature

nodes.definition: Compute P(A|B)=P(A∩B)/P(B), apply the chain rule, assess independence vs conditional independence for random variables.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new dependence structures encountered in practice

pros.claim: Enables decomposition of joint distributions via chain rule

cons.claim: Confusing independence with zero correlation causes severe downstream errors

failure_modes: confusing P(A|B) with P(B|A)
ignoring conditioning context in compound events
acceptance_tests: P(A|B) computed correctly on standard two-way tables
independence verified algebraically not just intuitively
revisit_triggers: new independence criteria added to syllabus
conditional vs marginal confusion observed in model outputs

nodes.definition: Apply Bayes' theorem P(H|E)∝P(E|H)P(H) for prior-to-posterior updating; distinguish likelihood, prior, posterior, and evidence normalizing constant.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new empirical evidence on human Bayesian reasoning or LLM Bayesian failures

pros.claim: Core reasoning engine for uncertainty quantification and belief updating under evidence

cons.claim: Ignoring priors (base-rate neglect) leads to systematically overconfident posteriors

failure_modes: neglecting base rate in low-prevalence scenarios
confusing P(E|H) with P(H|E) (prosecutor fallacy)
acceptance_tests: posterior computed correctly on canonical medical-test and spam-filter examples
base-rate neglect pitfall identified and corrected
revisit_triggers: base-rate neglect newly documented in field
Bayesian vs frequentist debate resurfaces in practitioner community

nodes.definition: Define discrete and continuous random variables; compute PMF/PDF/CDF; work with key named distributions: Binomial, Poisson, Geometric, Uniform, Normal, Exponential, Beta, Gamma.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new distribution families gaining prominence in ML (e.g., von Mises, Dirichlet variants)

pros.claim: Provides vocabulary for modeling real-world random phenomena compactly

cons.claim: Misidentifying distribution family leads to systematically wrong probability statements

failure_modes: using Normal for count data without checking Poisson/Binomial fit
confusing rate vs mean parameterization of Exponential
acceptance_tests: correct PMF/PDF stated for each named distribution
CDF derived from PDF by integration for continuous case
revisit_triggers: new canonical distribution added to practitioner toolkit
distribution parameterisation conventions change

nodes.definition: Compute E[X], Var(X)=E[X²]-(E[X])², higher moments, moment generating functions (MGF); apply linearity of expectation and law of total expectation.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new moment-based method gains traction in ML estimation literature

pros.claim: Linearity of expectation enables elegant solutions to complex counting and estimation problems

cons.claim: Forgetting non-linearity of variance under transformation causes systematic calibration errors

failure_modes: applying linearity of variance incorrectly to dependent variables
confusing variance with standard deviation in threshold problems
acceptance_tests: E[X] and Var(X) computed correctly for standard named distributions
law of total expectation applied correctly in iterated conditioning
revisit_triggers: MGF uniqueness theorem newly emphasized
law of total variance applications broadened

nodes.definition: Work with joint PMF/PDF, marginal and conditional distributions, covariance, correlation; multivariate Normal distribution and its properties.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new multivariate distribution families adopted in probabilistic ML frameworks

pros.claim: Enables modeling of dependent multi-dimensional data essential for multivariate ML

cons.claim: Ignoring covariance structure yields incorrect uncertainty propagation in multi-output models

failure_modes: treating correlated variables as independent
confusing zero correlation with independence for non-Normal cases
acceptance_tests: marginal derived correctly by integrating/summing out variables
bivariate Normal conditional derived correctly
revisit_triggers: multivariate distribution families expanded in practitioner use
new copula models emerge

nodes.definition: State and apply weak/strong LLN and CLT; understand convergence in probability vs distribution; quantify CLT approximation quality via Berry-Esseen.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: heavy-tailed distribution prevalence newly documented in practitioner data

pros.claim: Justifies sample mean as estimator and Normal approximation for inference

cons.claim: Applying CLT blindly to small n or heavy-tailed distributions produces dangerously wrong intervals

failure_modes: using CLT for n<30 with skewed data
confusing convergence in probability with almost-sure convergence
acceptance_tests: LLN demonstrated via simulation with convergence visualization
CLT approximation validated against exact binomial for n=30,100,500
revisit_triggers: Berry-Esseen bound newly required in practitioner curriculum
CLT failure conditions newly documented for heavy-tailed data

nodes.definition: Derive and compare point estimators using MLE, MOM, and Bayesian MAP; assess bias, variance, MSE, consistency, and efficiency; apply Cramér-Rao lower bound.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new loss-based estimation framework changes efficiency benchmarks

pros.claim: MLE provides statistically principled and asymptotically efficient parameter estimates

cons.claim: Biased estimator without correction yields systematically wrong parameter estimates in downstream ML

failure_modes: using biased sample variance (1/n) when unbiased (1/(n-1)) needed
treating MLE as always unbiased
acceptance_tests: MLE derived analytically for Bernoulli, Poisson, Normal
bias-variance decomposition computed for a given estimator
revisit_triggers: new estimation methods (e.g., M-estimators) gain prominence
Cramér-Rao bound extended to new family

nodes.definition: Construct confidence intervals for means, proportions, differences, and regression coefficients; interpret frequentist coverage correctly; compute required sample sizes.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: bootstrap and credible intervals increasingly preferred over classical CIs in practice

pros.claim: Provides honest uncertainty quantification around estimates required for sound decision-making

cons.claim: Misinterpreting CI as probability that parameter lies inside it causes systematic overconfidence

failure_modes: confusing CI coverage with posterior probability
using z-interval for small n with unknown variance
acceptance_tests: 95% CI for proportion interpreted correctly as coverage guarantee, not probability statement
t-interval vs z-interval boundary conditions articulated
revisit_triggers: CI interpretation widely misunderstood in ML literature
bootstrap CI methods newly added to core curriculum

nodes.definition: Formulate H0/H1, choose test statistic, compute p-value, control Type I/II errors, compute power; apply z, t, chi-squared, F tests; understand multiple testing corrections.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new multiple testing correction methods adopted in large-scale ML evaluation

pros.claim: Provides principled framework for distinguishing signal from noise in data

cons.claim: Misinterpreting p-value as posterior probability of null leads to rampant false discoveries

failure_modes: treating p<0.05 as proof of effect
ignoring power when interpreting null results
acceptance_tests: Type I and Type II error rates correctly specified for a given test
power computed for one-sample t-test given effect size and n
revisit_triggers: p-value misinterpretation newly documented
multiple testing burden increases in practitioner pipelines

nodes.definition: Perform full Bayesian inference: choose conjugate or non-conjugate priors, derive posterior, use MCMC/variational inference when closed form unavailable, compute credible intervals and posterior predictive distributions.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new probabilistic programming languages change Bayesian workflow best practices

pros.claim: Enables full uncertainty quantification coherent with probability theory for complex models

cons.claim: Improper prior or MCMC non-convergence yields invalid posteriors silently

failure_modes: using improper priors without checking propriety of posterior
declaring MCMC convergence from trace plot alone
acceptance_tests: posterior derived in closed form for conjugate Beta-Binomial and Normal-Normal pairs
credible interval correctly distinguished from frequentist CI
revisit_triggers: MCMC convergence diagnostics evolve
variational Bayes methods newly accessible via PPL frameworks

nodes.definition: Compute entropy H(X), KL-divergence KL(P‖Q), cross-entropy, mutual information I(X;Y); relate to maximum likelihood and variational inference objectives.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new generalized divergences adopted in normalizing flows or diffusion model objectives

pros.claim: KL divergence and cross-entropy connect probabilistic models to optimization objectives used in ML

cons.claim: Confusing KL direction KL(P‖Q) vs KL(Q‖P) leads to wrong VI or MLE equivalences

failure_modes: confusing cross-entropy with KL divergence
treating KL as symmetric
acceptance_tests: H(X) computed correctly for discrete distributions
KL(P‖Q) vs KL(Q‖P) asymmetry demonstrated on concrete example
revisit_triggers: information-theoretic ML objectives evolve
new divergences (alpha, Renyi) gain prominence

nodes.definition: Fit simple and multiple linear regression; interpret coefficients, R², residuals; assess assumptions (linearity, homoscedasticity, normality, independence); compute and interpret Pearson/Spearman correlation.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new regularized regression methods (Lasso/Ridge) supplant OLS as default in practitioner workflows

pros.claim: Linear regression is the canonical parametric estimation tool interpretable and diagnostically rich

cons.claim: Violating homoscedasticity assumption yields incorrect standard errors and invalid inference

failure_modes: ignoring multicollinearity inflating standard errors
extrapolating regression beyond support of training data
acceptance_tests: regression coefficients derived via OLS normal equations
assumptions (LLINCN) verified with diagnostic plots
revisit_triggers: robust regression methods newly emphasized
new collinearity diagnostics added to practitioner workflow

nodes.definition: Apply MC integration, importance sampling, rejection sampling, Markov Chain Monte Carlo (Metropolis-Hastings, Gibbs); assess convergence via Gelman-Rubin R-hat.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new gradient-based samplers change convergence diagnostics standards

pros.claim: MC methods enable intractable posterior and expectation computation in complex probabilistic models

cons.claim: Non-converged MCMC chains yield biased posterior estimates that look superficially plausible

failure_modes: using too-few MC samples without variance estimation
declaring convergence without R-hat check
acceptance_tests: MC integration error bound computed correctly via CLT
MCMC convergence assessed via R-hat < 1.05 criterion
revisit_triggers: new MCMC samplers (NUTS, HMC) become standard
importance weight degeneracy newly documented

nodes.definition: Identify and avoid common errors: p-hacking, multiple comparisons, survivorship bias, Simpson's paradox, Berkson's paradox, overfitting vs underfitting, and ecological fallacy.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new data collection biases or confounders documented in practitioner ML workflows

pros.claim: Awareness of canonical pitfalls prevents the most common and consequential statistical errors

cons.claim: Unrecognized Simpson's paradox or survivorship bias leads to inverted causal conclusions

failure_modes: attributing group-level patterns to individuals (ecological fallacy)
ignoring selection bias in observational data
acceptance_tests: Simpson's paradox demonstrated with numerical example and reversal explained
p-hacking mechanism explained and pre-registration described as mitigation
revisit_triggers: new statistical bias patterns documented in ML literature
new replication crisis findings emerge in practitioner-relevant domains

nodes.definition: Apply Markov, Chebyshev, Chernoff, Hoeffding, and McDiarmid inequalities for tail bound derivation; use in sample complexity and generalization bound proofs.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new matrix concentration inequalities adopted in deep learning theory

pros.claim: Concentration inequalities provide non-asymptotic sample complexity guarantees for ML

cons.claim: Using only asymptotic guarantees for finite samples yields dangerously optimistic generalization claims

failure_modes: applying Markov inequality to signed random variables
confusing union bound tightness with independence requirements
acceptance_tests: Chebyshev bound applied to compute minimum n for desired accuracy
Hoeffding inequality applied to bounded random variables correctly
revisit_triggers: new concentration inequalities adopted in PAC-learning literature
tighter bounds derived for specific ML architectures

nodes.definition: Distinguish correlation from causation; apply potential outcomes framework (Rubin) or DAG-based (Pearl do-calculus); understand confounders, instrumental variables, and RCT design.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new causal ML frameworks (Double ML, CausalML) become standard practitioner tools

pros.claim: Causal reasoning prevents drawing wrong action-oriented conclusions from observational data

cons.claim: Treating observational association as causal effect leads to harmful policy or model deployment decisions

failure_modes: ignoring confounders in observational study
using correlation-based feature importance as causal evidence
acceptance_tests: confounder identified correctly in a causal DAG
ATT vs ATE correctly distinguished in potential outcomes framework
revisit_triggers: new causal discovery algorithms emerge
do-calculus newly required in practitioner ML curricula

nodes.definition: Work with Bayesian networks and Markov random fields; perform variable elimination, belief propagation; understand d-separation and Markov blankets.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: deep generative models (VAE, diffusion) supersede classical PGMs in some practitioner workflows

pros.claim: Graphical models provide compact and interpretable representation of joint distributions over many variables

cons.claim: Failing to enforce Markov assumptions correctly leads to incorrect conditional independence claims

failure_modes: confusing Bayesian network with causal model
applying belief propagation on graphs with cycles
acceptance_tests: d-separation query answered correctly for a given DAG
variable elimination order computed and applied for simple Bayes net
revisit_triggers: new neural-network-based PGM hybrids emerge
d-separation algorithms updated in reference implementations

nodes.definition: Frame estimation and prediction as decision problems with loss functions; derive Bayes risk, minimax estimators; connect to regularization and shrinkage (James-Stein).

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new decision-theoretic frameworks for deep learning emerge in literature

pros.claim: Decision-theoretic framing unifies frequentist and Bayesian estimation under explicit loss

cons.claim: Optimizing wrong loss (e.g., 0-1 for regression) yields estimators misaligned with downstream cost

failure_modes: using mean when median minimizes L1 loss
optimizing surrogate loss without verifying alignment with true objective
acceptance_tests: Bayes estimator under squared error loss derived as posterior mean
minimax principle demonstrated on a concrete two-action problem
revisit_triggers: new loss functions adopted in ML practitioner toolkits
James-Stein shrinkage newly emphasised in high-dim settings

nodes.definition: Apply Bonferroni, Holm, Benjamini-Hochberg FDR procedures; understand FWER vs FDR distinction; design experiments accounting for multiple comparisons in ML evaluation.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new selective inference methods adopted in post-hoc ML analysis

pros.claim: FDR control enables principled large-scale hypothesis testing without excessive false positives

cons.claim: Ignoring multiple testing inflation yields an epidemic of spurious significant findings

failure_modes: applying Bonferroni when tests are positively correlated (overly conservative)
treating BH FDR rejection as individual null being true
acceptance_tests: BH procedure applied correctly on a ranked p-value list
FWER vs FDR tradeoff articulated for a given experimental context
revisit_triggers: new FDR procedures adopted for high-dimensional ML evaluation
q-value methods newly emphasised in practitioner toolkits

nodes.definition: Apply nonparametric and parametric bootstrap for SE estimation, CI construction, and hypothesis testing; understand when bootstrap fails (heavy tails, small n, non-smooth statistics).

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new conformal prediction methods supplant bootstrap for coverage guarantees in ML

pros.claim: Bootstrap provides distribution-free uncertainty quantification without closed-form assumptions

cons.claim: Bootstrap fails silently for non-smooth statistics or heavy-tailed distributions giving misleading CIs

failure_modes: using standard bootstrap for time series without block structure
using too-few bootstrap replicates (B<200) for tail quantile estimation
acceptance_tests: bootstrap CI computed for a median estimate and compared to normal-theory CI
bootstrap failure condition (max statistic with heavy tail) identified
revisit_triggers: new bootstrap variants (wild, block) newly emphasised
bootstrap failure regimes newly documented

nodes.definition: Apply statistical methods to LLM evaluation: power analysis for benchmark comparisons, bootstrap CIs for win rates, multiple comparison corrections across benchmarks, calibration assessment (ECE/Brier score).

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new LLM evaluation protocols adopted that change statistical requirements

pros.claim: Rigorous statistical design of LLM evaluations prevents false claims of model superiority

cons.claim: Under-powered LLM benchmark comparisons yield noisy rankings that mislead model selection decisions

failure_modes: comparing LLM benchmarks without multiple-testing correction
treating LLM win-rate point estimate as definitive without CI
acceptance_tests: power analysis run before benchmark comparison to confirm detectable effect size
ECE computed correctly from binned prediction probabilities
revisit_triggers: LLM evaluation methodology evolves
new calibration metrics adopted in practitioner benchmarks

nodes.definition: Define sufficient statistics via Fisher-Neyman factorization; identify minimal sufficient statistics; work with exponential family distributions and their natural parameters.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: information geometry and natural gradient frameworks gain traction in ML optimisation

pros.claim: Exponential families unify MLE, natural gradient, and variational inference in a common framework

cons.claim: Ignoring sufficient statistic structure leads to inefficient estimators with avoidable variance

failure_modes: using non-sufficient statistic for inference when sufficient one exists
misidentifying natural parameter in exponential family parameterization
acceptance_tests: sufficiency verified via factorization theorem for Bernoulli and Normal
exponential family canonical form identified for Poisson and Gamma
revisit_triggers: new exponential family members adopted in ML models
Fisher information geometry newly emphasised

nodes.definition: Apply rank-based tests (Mann-Whitney, Wilcoxon, Kruskal-Wallis), kernel density estimation, and empirical CDF; understand power vs parametric alternatives.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: conformal prediction methods adopted as new standard for distribution-free inference

pros.claim: Distribution-free tests provide valid inference without Normality assumptions

cons.claim: Using parametric t-test on ordinal or non-Normal data yields invalid significance claims

failure_modes: confusing nonparametric with assumption-free (still require independence)
over-smoothing KDE masking multimodality
acceptance_tests: Mann-Whitney U test applied correctly with tie handling
KDE bandwidth selection via cross-validation demonstrated
revisit_triggers: new nonparametric tests gain adoption for LLM evaluation
conformal prediction newly bridges nonparametric and frequentist inference

edges.resolution_rule: Use Bayesian credible intervals for decision-making when prior information is strong; use frequentist testing when long-run error control is required by stakeholders
Prefer analytical posteriors when conjugate; use MCMC only when posterior is intractable and document convergence diagnostics

conflict_axes.description: Frequentist error-rate control vs Bayesian coherent belief updating as primary inference paradigm
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: Choose based on whether long-run calibration or coherent belief updating is the primary requirement; document choice explicitly

conflict_axes.description: Parametric distributional assumptions enable efficiency but fail when assumptions violated; nonparametric methods are robust but less powerful
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: Default to parametric when diagnostics support assumptions; fall back to nonparametric when assumption violations are detected

conflict_axes.description: Asymptotic guarantees (CLT, MLE) are tractable but unreliable at small n; finite-sample bounds (Hoeffding, Berry-Esseen) are valid but conservative
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: Use finite-sample bounds for safety-critical claims; use asymptotics for exploration and direction

conflict_axes.description: Statistical significance (p-value) can be achieved with negligible effect size at large n; practical significance requires effect size estimation
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: Always report effect sizes and CIs alongside p-values; do not gate decisions on significance alone

conflict_axes.description: Observational correlation is insufficient for causal conclusions; causal inference requires additional structure (DAG, RCT, IV)
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: Use causal DAG to identify confounders before attributing effect to a variable

conflict_axes.description: Informative priors improve efficiency but introduce subjectivity; flat priors are defensible but may be improper or poorly calibrated
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: Perform prior sensitivity analysis; document prior choice rationale and check posterior propriety

conflict_axes.description: MCMC provides asymptotically exact posteriors but is slow; variational inference is fast but biased toward underestimating variance
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: Use VI for exploration and large models; use MCMC with convergence diagnostics for final inference

conflict_axes.description: FWER control (Bonferroni) is conservative with many tests; FDR control (BH) allows more discoveries at cost of per-comparison error control
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: Use FWER when any single false positive is costly; use FDR for exploratory large-scale comparison

conflict_axes.description: Complex probabilistic models (PGMs, hierarchical Bayes) fit data better but are harder to audit and debug
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: Start with simpler interpretable models; add complexity only when simpler model fails diagnostic checks

conflict_axes.description: Using training data statistics to choose statistical tests for LLM evaluation inflates apparent performance (Goodhart's law)
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: Pre-register evaluation protocol; use held-out benchmark sets; apply multiple-testing corrections across all comparisons

edge_cases.description: Confusing P(evidence|innocent) with P(innocent|evidence) in legal or diagnostic contexts
edge_cases.mitigation: Apply Bayes' theorem explicitly with base rate; never report likelihood alone as posterior probability

edge_cases.description: Aggregate trend reverses direction within subgroups due to confounding variable
edge_cases.mitigation: Stratify analysis by confounder; use causal DAG to identify correct conditioning set

edge_cases.description: Analyzing only successes while failures are unobserved leads to systematically optimistic conclusions
edge_cases.mitigation: Explicitly characterize selection mechanism; include failure data or model selection process

edge_cases.description: Normal approximation via CLT fails for distributions with infinite variance (Cauchy, Pareto with alpha<2)
edge_cases.mitigation: Use heavy-tail diagnostics (Hill estimator, QQ plot); apply stable distribution or robust methods

edge_cases.description: Post-hoc hypothesis generation after data inspection inflates false discovery rate
edge_cases.mitigation: Pre-register hypotheses and analysis plan; apply multiple comparison corrections for all tested hypotheses

edge_cases.description: Flat improper prior yields improper posterior for some likelihood-prior combinations
edge_cases.mitigation: Verify posterior propriety analytically before MCMC; use weakly informative proper priors by default

edge_cases.description: Bootstrap underestimates variance of maximum-order statistics in heavy-tailed distributions
edge_cases.mitigation: Use m-out-of-n bootstrap or extreme value theory for max statistics

edge_cases.description: MCMC chain has not reached stationary distribution; samples biased toward initial region
edge_cases.mitigation: Run multiple chains; check R-hat<1.05 and ESS>400; discard burn-in; visualize trace plots

edge_cases.description: Drawing individual-level inferences from group-level statistics
edge_cases.mitigation: Use individual-level data for individual inferences; specify level of analysis explicitly

edge_cases.description: Model confidence scores systematically misaligned with empirical frequencies
edge_cases.mitigation: Compute reliability diagrams and ECE; apply Platt scaling or isotonic regression for recalibration

edge_cases.description: Comparing LLMs across 10+ benchmarks without correction yields spurious SOTA claims
edge_cases.mitigation: Apply Benjamini-Hochberg or Bonferroni correction across all benchmarks simultaneously

edge_cases.description: Pre-training data overlap between model versions confounds performance comparison
edge_cases.mitigation: Control for data contamination; use held-out benchmark or randomized ablation

workflow.description: Specify sample space Omega, event sigma-algebra, and probability measure P satisfying Kolmogorov axioms
workflow.gate: axioms verified; probability measure sums/integrates to 1

workflow.description: Identify appropriate named distribution family for each random variable based on support and generating process
Derive expectation, variance, and relevant higher moments; apply law of total expectation for iterated conditioning
workflow.gate: linearity of expectation applied correctly; variance non-linearity documented

workflow.description: Decide whether question is estimation, testing, or prediction; choose frequentist vs Bayesian framework; document decision rationale
workflow.gate: CA_01 conflict axis consulted; framework chosen explicitly

workflow.description: Derive MLE or MAP estimator; verify bias, consistency, and efficiency; check Cramér-Rao lower bound
workflow.gate: at least one optimality property verified; Cramér-Rao bound computed if tractable

workflow.description: Build CI or credible interval; interpret correctly per chosen framework; compute required n if planning
workflow.gate: CI coverage semantics correctly stated; credible interval vs CI distinction explicit

workflow.description: Formulate H0/H1; choose test statistic; compute p-value; apply multiple comparison correction if multiple tests
workflow.gate: all tests enumerated before correction applied; effect size reported alongside p-value

workflow.description: Choose prior; compute or sample posterior; verify convergence (R-hat for MCMC); compute posterior predictive
workflow.gate: prior propriety verified; MCMC R-hat<1.05 if sampling used

workflow.description: Draw causal DAG; identify confounders and mediators; choose identification strategy (adjustment, IV, RCT)
workflow.gate: CA_05 conflict axis applied; confounders explicitly identified

workflow.description: Check analysis against canonical pitfalls: Simpson's paradox, survivorship bias, p-hacking, multiple testing, calibration
workflow.gate: all edge cases EC_01 through EC_12 consulted; mitigations documented

workflow.description: Run power analysis for benchmark comparison; choose correction method; compute bootstrap CIs for win rates; assess calibration
workflow.gate: multiple benchmarks corrected; power>=0.80; ECE reported

workflow.description: Document all statistical choices, assumptions, results, and limitations; lock analysis before sharing
workflow.gate: all CA conflict axes addressed; all EC edge cases checked; human_review_required nodes reviewed

dominance_rules.rationale: High-risk nodes (probability foundations, pitfalls, Bayes, hypothesis testing, LLM eval) must have verifiable acceptance criteria reviewed by domain expert

dominance_rules.action: prefer Bayesian credible interval over p-value
dominance_rules.rationale: When strong prior exists and Bayesian semantics are acceptable, credible intervals are more interpretable and coherent
Parametric assumptions fail for small skewed samples; distribution-free tests provide valid inference

dominance_rules.action: apply multiple comparison correction before reporting rejections
dominance_rules.rationale: Each untreated additional test inflates FWER; correction is non-negotiable for valid inference

dominance_rules.action: block posterior inference until R-hat<1.05 and ESS>400
dominance_rules.rationale: Non-converged chains produce biased samples; downstream inference is invalid regardless of model correctness

dominance_rules.action: require causal DAG and confounder identification before claim
dominance_rules.rationale: Observational associations cannot support causal conclusions without explicit identification strategy
Standard bootstrap undercovers for extreme statistics; EVT or m-out-of-n provides valid CI
LLM evaluation across multiple benchmarks without correction yields Goodhart-inflated SOTA claims
Improper posteriors produce meaningless credible intervals; propriety must be verified before sampling
p-value alone is uninformative about practical significance; effect size and CI are mandatory
CLT approximation is unreliable for small skewed samples; exact or resampling methods required
Highly coupled nodes propagate errors across the KB; revisit conditions must be explicit

anti_rework_rules.rationale: Changing sample space invalidates all downstream estimators; lock probability space before deriving estimators
Switching frequentist/Bayesian after seeing data is post-hoc analysis; framework choice must be pre-data
Post-hoc hypothesis addition (HARKing) inflates false discovery rate; all hypotheses must be pre-registered
Re-running without checking R-hat wastes compute and may mask persistent non-convergence
Iterative refitting on residuals is model selection without correction; use proper model selection criteria (AIC/BIC) or split data
Choosing correction method after seeing p-values to maximize rejections is p-hacking by another name
Prior revision after data examination destroys Bayesian coherence; prior must be specified before data analysis
CLT requires finite variance; applying to Cauchy or Pareto(alpha<2) produces invalid normal approximations
Observational vs experimental distinction determines valid causal claims; cannot be changed after data collection
Each documented edge case represents a high-frequency practitioner error; skipping audit risks shipping flawed analysis
Uncertainty quantification is mandatory; bare point estimates mislead consumers of statistical analysis

iteration_protocol.action: consult CA_01 frequentist_vs_bayesian axis; re-examine stakeholder requirements; document final choice with rationale before proceeding
apply nonparametric test or bootstrap; revisit REGRESSION and NONPARAM nodes; recheck acceptance tests
extend chains; check for multi-modality; reparameterize model; re-run diagnostics before any inference
rebuild causal DAG; re-identify adjustment set; rerun estimation with correct conditioning; flag prior results as preliminary
enumerate all tests conducted; apply BH or Bonferroni as appropriate; revise rejection decisions; update MULTITEST node
diagnose heavy tail or small n; switch to m-out-of-n bootstrap or EVT; revisit BOOTSTRAP and PROB_INEQ
apply recalibration (Platt scaling / isotonic regression); recompute ECE; update PROB_LLM acceptance tests
stratify by confounding variable; apply CAUSAL_INF identification strategy; revise conclusions
switch to sufficient-statistic-based estimator for efficiency gain; recheck Cramér-Rao bound
check for benchmark contamination; revisit power analysis; apply causal reasoning to identify source of discrepancy

priority_rationale: Priority ordered by foundational dependency and practitioner impact: probability foundations first, then conditional probability and Bayes as the core reasoning engine, then distributions and expectation, then limit theorems enabling inference, then pitfall awareness (high risk_if_wrong), then hypothesis testing and Bayesian inference, then LLM-specific application, then causal reasoning and regression, then advanced methods (PGMs, stochastic processes, asymptotic theory).
